featured_reviews.review_text:
I added two stars for the good owners. The guy present in the store is an extremely cranky and irritable person. Last year, I purchased a large beautiful seated Ganesha with led lighting and 5 brass Hindu idols. Gave them Rs.25k worth of business in one order. At the time of selling, the cranky man had said the metallic gold paint on the Ganesha's garments will not get tarnished. But it started turning black in just 6 months. When I visited him today, I showed him pictures of the blackened paint and asked him the remedy. I had not uttered the word guarantee or warranty, I simply and calmly asked him what's the solution. And he started rudely telling me in a loud voice that there is no warranty or guarantee for any items in the store. I again asked him what's the solution and I understand there's nothing like a warranty for the art items. But he should offer a solution since he had claimed the paint will not fade or get tarnished. He again started almost shouting that I will never give warranty or guarantee. If you want to get it repainted, you have to pay the artists fees. I said ok what would be the approximate fees. Again screamed, How will I know? Artist is not available now. When he will be back, you have to pay whatever he asks for. And he did this ruckus in front of other customers in the shop potentially jeopardizing future sales.

I told him I will not shop there again left the store as I didn't want to traumatize my daughter who was with me. Even as we were leaving, the guy said, your choice don't come here again.

Apart from this negative experience with the cranky man, the store has beautiful artworks and the owners are decent people. Last year, they delivered the Ganesha to our home carefully so that we don't need to worry about damaging it while taking it home. So two stars to the owners. But zero for the cranky store guy.

featured_reviews.name: Sahil Agarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Team Drapednuts,

Since your response attempts to reframe the situation, it is important—for the awareness of everyone reading—to clarify what actually transpired.

The **initial delivery was a complete failure** and unfit for a wedding event. My wife was extremely disappointed, and only after that did I contact you. During that conversation, you spoke politely and **acknowledged the issue**, agreed to redesign the product, and assured step-by-step updates.

However, the very next day, when I reminded you that the invite was **urgently required on the mutually agreed date**, your approach changed entirely. Despite having taken **100% advance**, you outright refused any refund—something that is neither customer-friendly nor standard practice in any professional industry.

With no time left and no alternative, I was forced to proceed. What followed was **not a fresh redesign**, but only **minor alterations to the same substandard piece**. When I asked for proper cosmetic and finishing changes, I was repeatedly told it was “not possible,” would “take too much time,” and other vague justifications.

To be very clear:
**Final acceptance under pressure and helplessness should not be misrepresented as satisfaction.**

Additionally, due to **poor coordination and repeated back-and-forth caused by your own shortcomings**, I had to pay **porter/delivery charges multiple times**, further adding to the inconvenience and cost.

Regarding your comment about taking this public instead of communicating directly:
**I did communicate directly—multiple times.** Unfortunately, those conversations led to assurances without outcomes, refusals of refunds, and forced compromises. Public feedback exists precisely for situations where private communication fails to resolve genuine issues. Transparency works both ways, not only when it favors the seller.

Design preferences may be subjective, but **quality, craftsmanship, accountability, and value for money are not**. This experience failed on all counts and **genuinely ruined the charm of an important family event**.

This response is not written out of spite, but out of responsibility—so future customers can make informed decisions.

— Sahil

Overall, this was a very disappointing experience. Overpriced, poor quality, and a complete mismatch between expectations and delivery. I would not recommend Draped Dryfruits to anyone looking for meaningful, well-crafted wedding invitations.
